claims.statement: The Java code is layered into eight packages under com.caozhihu.tmall — action, service, service.impl, dao.impl, pojo, interceptor, util and test — and the Spring configuration consumes those trees directly: <context:component-scan base-package="com.caozhihu.tmall.*"/> collects the @Service/@Component/@Repository beans and packagesToScan com.caozhihu.* collects the entities, so a class placed outside them is never wired or mapped.

Dependency direction between the layers: the action package imports service interfaces, pojo and util but never service.impl or dao.impl; service.impl is the single package that imports dao.impl; and the only reverse (pojo to service) edge is Order importing OrderService for its status strings.

src/ is the only source root: the embedded launcher compiles every .java under src/ into web/WEB-INF/classes and copies the non-Java resources on each start, so new classes must be placed under src/com/caozhihu/tmall/<package>/ and web/WEB-INF/classes is disposable build output rather than a place to edit.

An HTTP endpoint exists only as the string on an @Action-annotated method: src/struts.xml declares no <action> element and only the basicstruts package, plus the encoding and Spring object-factory constants, so URLs, result names and views are defined entirely in annotations and JSP files.

Every concrete action class in the repository — CategoryAction, ProductAction, ProductImageAction, PropertyAction, PropertyValueAction, UserAction, OrderAction and ForeAction — extends Action4Result, and between them they declare 47 @Action methods.

Actions inherit everything they need by extending Action4Result, because the chain is ordered Action4Upload to Action4Pagination to Action4Pojo to Action4Service to Action4Parameter to Action4Result: upload binding fields, the Page field, the entity and collection fields, service access with t2p()/saveWithJpg(), the loose request parameters, and the shared result catalogue.

Action4Result carries @Namespace("/"), @ParentPackage("basicstruts") and the entire @Result catalogue for both the back office and the storefront while its own body is empty; subclasses therefore return bare result-name strings (CategoryAction.list returns "listCategory" without declaring any result), and the recorded acceptance run confirms the arrangement renders end to end.

@ParentPackage("basicstruts") is the link between an action and src/struts.xml: that package sets <default-interceptor-ref name="auth-dafault">, so an action that does not inherit the annotation runs without the authority, category-names and cart-count interceptors.

The service-layer file pair is fixed: an interface XxxService extends BaseService in com.caozhihu.tmall.service and an implementation XxxServiceImpl extends BaseServiceImpl implements XxxService in com.caozhihu.tmall.service.impl annotated @Service("xxxService"); for an entity with only inherited CRUD both classes contain no methods at all.

BaseServiceImpl's constructor derives each service's entity class from the name of the instantiating subclass by reading a deliberately thrown exception's stack trace: it strips the ServiceImpl suffix to obtain the entity simple name and rewrites the .service.impl package to the sibling .pojo package, so a working service implementation must be named XxxServiceImpl with its entity class Xxx placed in the corresponding .pojo package.

The derived clazz field is protected with a single assignment and no setter or override, so breaking the XxxServiceImpl / pojo.Xxx pairing surfaces only as a printed ClassNotFoundException followed by a null clazz failure at the first query, not as a container wiring error.

Action4Service is the only @Component in the action package, and the nine @Autowired service properties it declares (categoryService, propertyService, productService, productImageService, propertyValueService, userService, orderService, orderItemService, reviewService) carry the same names as the @Service bean names on the implementations.

Action4Service supplies the inherited helpers every action may use: t2p(Object), which reloads an id-only request parameter into a persistent entity through the service and reflects it back onto the action's own setXxx method, and saveWithJpg(File), which copies the bound upload and rewrites it as JPEG.

Domain-specific service behaviour is declared on the entity's XxxService interface and implemented in XxxServiceImpl (ProductService.search, OrderService.createOrder, OrderItemService.fill), and one service may inject others (ProductServiceImpl injects ProductImageService, OrderItemService and ReviewService) rather than reaching into another layer.

Domain status and type strings are public static final String constants declared on the service interfaces — OrderService.waitPay through delete, and ProductImageService.type_single / type_detail — and other layers reference those constants instead of repeating the literals.

Transactionality is annotation-driven rather than wrapped in a service facade: applicationContext.xml enables <tx:annotation-driven transaction-manager="transactionManager"/>, BaseServiceImpl.save is annotated @Transactional, and specific multi-row write paths add @Transactional(readOnly = false) (PropertyValueServiceImpl.init, PropertyAction.add).

Data access is reached by delegation rather than by injecting the DAO: DAOImpl is the only DAO class (@Repository("dao"), extends HibernateTemplate, no interface above it), ServiceDelegateDAO holds @Resource(name = "dao") DAOImpl and forwards every HibernateTemplate operation, and BaseServiceImpl extends ServiceDelegateDAO so services call findByCriteria/find/save/update/delete as their own methods; a new data operation becomes available by adding one more forwarding method to ServiceDelegateDAO.

Entities live in com.caozhihu.tmall.pojo and follow one annotation shape: @Entity with @Table(name = ...), an int id carrying @Id, @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY) and @Column, @ManyToOne with @JoinColumn(name = <column in the SQL script>) for relations, and @Transient for view-only fields that services fill.

A relation property must be named exactly the uncapitalized class name of the parent entity, because BaseServiceImpl.listByParent, list(Page, Object) and total(Object) build their criteria and HQL from StringUtils.uncapitalize(parent.getClass().getSimpleName()) — as product, category, order, user and property do in the shipped entities.

Persistent column names equal the Java field names in camelCase (product.subTitle, product.originalPrice, product.remark, order_.orderCode, order_.createDate), and because hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto is none while the schema is created by the dbInit DataSourceInitializer executing src/sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql at context start, adding a table, column or foreign key means editing that script rather than relying on Hibernate; the one column added to an existing table so far, product.remark, was appended with ALTER TABLE after that table's seeded INSERT block instead of being folded into its CREATE TABLE, and no service, action or DAO class needs a change for such a field.

Table-name spelling is not uniform between the entities and the initialisation script — @Table names include order_, productImage and orderItem while the script creates order_, productimage and orderitem — and both resolve because H2 treats unquoted identifiers case-insensitively.

Interceptors live in com.caozhihu.tmall.interceptor, extend com.opensymphony.xwork2.interceptor.AbstractInterceptor and may @Autowired services, but an interceptor is inert unless it is both declared as an <interceptor> in src/struts.xml and referenced inside the <interceptor-stack name="auth-dafault"> that is the basicstruts package default; the misspelled stack name is a string contract referenced in exactly those two places.

AuthInterceptor gates only URIs starting with /fore, matching the URI remainder after the last "/fore" against the hard-coded array {home, checkLogin, register, login, loginAjax, product, category, search}; every other /fore URL requires the session attribute user or the client is redirected to login.jsp, so a new publicly reachable storefront endpoint must add its suffix to that array.

AuthInterceptor evaluates the raw request URI (it computes contextPath but never uses it), whereas CategoryNamesBelowSearchInterceptor and CartTotalItemNumberInterceptor strip the context path before comparing, so the authority check only holds while the application is served as the root context — which the embedded launcher does.

The interceptors publish the session attributes that the JSP fragments read — cs (the category list below the search box, from CategoryNamesBelowSearchInterceptor) and cartTotalItemNumber (the cart badge, from CartTotalItemNumberInterceptor) — so renaming either key is a cross-layer change rather than a local edit.

com.caozhihu.tmall.util holds the two unannotated cross-layer helpers: Page, whose count defaults to 5 and whose start/count/total/param/getTotalPage/getLast/isHasPreviouse/isHasNext contract is what the pager fragment web/include/admin/adminPage.jsp renders, and ImageUtil, whose conversion and resize methods are static.

Tests belong to com.caozhihu.tmall.test and follow one pattern — JUnit 4 with @RunWith(SpringJUnit4ClassRunner.class), @ContextConfiguration("classpath:applicationContext.xml"), @Test @Transactional methods and @Autowired beans — and because the launcher compiles everything under src/ into web/WEB-INF/classes, a new test joins the deployed compilation and must stay within the vendored web/WEB-INF/lib classpath; no build file or test task exists.

The back-office convention is one XxxAction per entity exposing the five @Action URLs admin_xxx_list, admin_xxx_add, admin_xxx_edit, admin_xxx_update and admin_xxx_delete; list and edit forward to the result names listXxx and editXxx (resolving to /admin/listXxx.jsp and /admin/editXxx.jsp), while add, update and delete return listXxxPage, a redirect back to the list URL that carries the parent id through OGNL for parent-scoped lists.

A parent-scoped admin list stores its parent key in the Page bean with page.setParam (for example "&category.id=" + category.getId()) so the pager links keep the parent id, and the pager fragment renders from page.start/count/total/totalPage/hasPreviouse/hasNext plus that param.

Admin forms bind entity fields as OGNL property paths on the inherited action fields (name="category.name", name="product.category.id", name="product.remark", uploads always name="img"), pass the entity id and the parent id in hidden inputs to the add/update URLs, and use deleteLink="true" anchors whose confirmation is implemented in web/include/admin/adminHeader.jsp; no server-side field validation exists.

A new storefront endpoint is a @Action("fore<verbInCamelCase>") method on ForeAction (the single class holding all 24 fore… endpoints), returning either "<page>.jsp" against a forward @Result whose location is /<page>.jsp, or "<name>Page" against a redirect @Result whose location carries ids as OGNL (forebuy?oiids=${oiid}, forealipay?order.id=${order.id}&total=${total}).

A new storefront view is a page JSP at web/<page>.jsp holding only the page directive plus the fixed include order include/header.jsp, include/top.jsp, include/search.jsp (or include/simpleSearch.jsp), include/<domain>/<name>Page.jsp, include/footer.jsp, with the page's own markup living in the include/<domain>/ fragment named after the page it backs.

Storefront state that must survive across requests is kept in existing session attributes (user, cs, cartTotalItemNumber, orderItems) rather than in new ad-hoc attributes, which is how the cart, checkout and review flows hand data between actions.

The repository records this checkout as an SDD rehearsal on an existing project and states that the original business Java, JSPs, web.xml, directory structure and Action/Service/DAO/entity classes were left unchanged; MIGRATION.md's acceptance table (one-command start without Tomcat or MySQL, /forehome and /admin_category_list returning 200, static resources, H2 console) is the only recorded end-to-end verification evidence in the repository.

README.md's description has drifted from the current code: it states that Action4Result extends Action4Service although the code inserts Action4Parameter in between, it attributes upload handling to Action4Upload although saveWithJpg is declared on Action4Service, and it frames the runtime as Tomcat with MySQL while this checkout runs embedded Jetty with an H2 in-memory database.

Nothing in the deployment descriptor gates the back office: web/WEB-INF/web.xml declares only the Struts2 and character-encoding filters mapped to /*, the Spring ContextLoaderListener and contextConfigLocation — no security-constraint, no login-config and no welcome-file list — and AuthInterceptor inspects only /fore URIs, so no admin_* URL is authenticated.

A new admin list page repeats the shipped composition: the ../include/admin/adminHeader.jsp and adminNavigator.jsp includes, a data table over the list collection, a div.pageDiv wrapping the adminPage.jsp pager fragment when the list is paged, and an add form posting to admin_xxx_add.

The repository's shipped example of the two-file rule reaches its column only through the admin product screens with no code-layer change: the name remark appears in Product.java, src/sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql, the add form input name="product.remark", the edit form echo value="${product.remark}" and the list cell ${p.remark}, and in no service, action, DAO or storefront file.

The seed script's own header comment lists only four syntactic adaptations of the original MySQL script and asserts that the business table structures and data were unchanged, while the file also appends ALTER TABLE product ADD COLUMN remark varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL;, leaving the seeded product table with a column its CREATE TABLE never declares; the page records this as a review item 【人工评审待确认】 asking whether the comment must list such structural appends and whether appending is the standing convention for a later column.
